title: Air Force Civil Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: Design Build Construction for Selective Improvement Project in Hong Kong Consulate � Sources Sought/Market Research
description: Department of State 2027 Design-Build Construction for Hong Kong Existing Consulate Compound (ECC) Selective Improvements Project (SIP) Sources Sought Market Research This is a Sources Sought Notice Only. This Sources Sought Notice is issued for information and planning purposes only as part of U.S. Department of State market research and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP). The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified businesses, with a special interest in Small Business (SB), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a), and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms under NAICS code 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Be advised that acquisition strategy and set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government is requesting information regarding the availability of capable firms to support the requirements of the U.S. Department of State (DOS), Bureau of Overseas Buildings Operations (OBO) for a Design-Build (DB) construction contract at the existing U.S. Consulate General compound in Hong Kong, S.A.R., China. Please note that a decision not to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice will not preclude a vendor from participating in any future solicitation. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice, nor will it compensate responders for any costs incurred in the development or furnishing of a response. 1. Project Description � Hong Kong Existing Consulate Compound (ECC) Selective Improvements Project (SIP), Design-Build Construction TOP SECRET FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCES ARE REQUIRED. A Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Top-Secret facility security clearance (FCL) with Secret safeguarding capability is required for this project, along with an OBO/SPC approved dedicated project space, OBO/DT-approved classified Information System (IS) and ProjNet-C for handling classified information up to the Secret level. Property Description: The project is located at the existing U.S. Consulate General compound, 26 Garden Rd, Central, Hong Kong. The site comprises 1.42 acres in the Central Business District of Hong Kong and is bounded along its perimeter by Garden Rd, Lower Albert Rd, and Upper Albert Rd. The site is fully developed and occupied. Background: The Design-Build solicitation will follow a bridging design effort (Task Order awarded to an A/E IDIQ contractor) that is developing concept, Design Intent 1 (DI-1), and Design Intent 2 (DI-2) design packages to support an eventual Design-Build Request for Proposal. Project Scope: The project will address deficiencies in life safety, infrastructure, and space utilization at the existing, occupied consulate compound. Key scope elements may include: Provide code-compliant emergency egress and fire sprinkler piping Replace/add chillers and other mechanical infrastructure (air-handling units, Building Automation System) Upgrade electrical and telecommunications infrastructure Provide accessible pathways for all consular functions Improve space utilization Replace roof and repair minor structural deficiencies Important and Unique Considerations: This project requires phasing and logistics to maintain existing post operations with minimal disruption, as the compound must remain fully functional throughout construction. The Design-Build offeror will be expected to develop a constructability analysis, phasing plan, and project execution schedule showing how work will be accomplished with limited swing space and very limited on-site storage/laydown area in an occupied, secure diplomatic facility. Estimated Construction Cost & Contract Type: The design-build project is currently estimated to be between $65,000,000 - $95,000,000, representing the estimated construction cost at award, inclusive of all direct and indirect costs to be incurred by the General Contractor for full delivery of the project scope. The contract type for this project is Firm-Fixed Price. Estimated Design-Build Contract Period: The related Bridging Design task order period runs September 2026 through July 2027. The anticipated design/build construction duration is approximately four years, with award planned for early FY2028. 2. Capability Statement Requirements Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11-inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide all the following requested information: a) Company information � Company name, System for Award Management Unique Entity Identification number (SAM UEI), address, point of contact name, phone number, and email address. b) Company's business size and socioeconomic status for the applicable NAICS code 236220, such as: Certified HUBZone, Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), 8(a) Participant, Small Business, or Other than Small Business (Large Business). c) Experience and capability � Provide experience and demonstrate capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past eight (8) years. Each example should include: i. A brief description of the project ii. Description of the work performed, including identification of self-performance and/or subcontractor management iii. Customer name iv. Timeliness of performance v. Dollar value of the project vi. Any challenges experienced during the project, including delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management or organizational issues, or other significant challenges Given the classified/secure and occupied-facility nature of this project, firms should also highlight experience with: Design-Build construction in occupied, secure U.S. diplomatic or comparably classified facilities Personnel holding or able to obtain DCSA Top Secret facility and personnel security clearances Overseas construction logistics, phasing, and limited-laydown-area execution d) Bonding capability � Provide bonding capability in the form of a surety letter. Please submit all capability statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page maximum above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Responses will not restrict the Government to any particular acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. 3. Closing Deadline for Submissions ALL ELECTRONIC SUBMISSIONS MUST BE RECEIVED BY 2:00 P.M. Eastern Time on December 01, 2026. Please provide submission responses and/or questions via email to Lenny Le at LELT@state.gov and Patrick Reilly at reillypa2@state.gov.

title: National Coast Guard Museum- Facility Maintenance Services
description: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, including small businesses (such as 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB), to provide comprehensive 24/7 Facility Maintenance services for the newly constructed National Coast Guard Museum in New London, Connecticut. The selected contractor will be required to furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, and materials necessary to ensure safe, reliable, and compliant museum operations. The facility consists of an 84,000 sq. ft., six-story waterfront building situated on under 1 acre of grounds. Core requirements include, but are not limited to: HVAC & Environmental Controls: Continuous operation and maintenance of gas-fired condensing boilers, chillers, cooling towers, radiant flooring, and Building Automation Systems (BAS) to maintain strict gallery climate tolerances (68�F�72�F and 45%�55% Relative Humidity). Electrical, Plumbing, & Life Safety: Operations and maintenance of power distribution panels, emergency generators, fuel systems, fire alarms, fire extinguishers (NFPA 10), and water sprinkler systems (NFPA 25). Vertical Transportation: Monthly servicing, emergency response, and annual certified load testing for four (4) elevators. Custodial Services: A hybrid staffing model providing APPA Level 1 (Orderly Spotlessness) cleaning standards in high-traffic public galleries and APPA Level 4 in back-of-house staff areas. Grounds, Hardscape, & Snow Removal: Year-round exterior upkeep, power washing, and 24/7 bare-pavement snow and ice control (utilizing hardscape-safe compounds) for walkways, terraces, and flat roofing. Support Services: Integrated Pest Management (artifact-safe), catering kitchen equipment upkeep, and refuse/recycling stream management. Note: Museum artifacts, exhibit curation, and IT network infrastructure are excluded from this scope. See attachments for additional details

title: Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction - NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1)
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction Project NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000003, located in Dutchess, Nassau, Suffolk and Saratoga Counties, New York; Sullivan County, New Hampshire; and Hampden County, Massachusetts. The project consists of bridge maintenance and pavement preservation of roadways and parking areas across several parks including Home of FDR National Historic Site (HOFR), Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site (ELRO), Vanderbuilt Mansion National Historic Site (VAMA), Fire Island National Seashore (FIIS), Saint Gaudens National Historic Park (SAGA), Sagamore Hill National Historic Park (SAHI), Saratoga National Historical Park (SARA) and Springfield Armory National Historical Park (SPAR). The work includes thin lift asphalt overlay, chip seal, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, pavement markings, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. title: National Coast Guard Museum- Facility Maintenance Services
description: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, including small businesses (such as 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB), to provide comprehensive 24/7 Facility Maintenance services for the newly constructed National Coast Guard Museum in New London, Connecticut. The selected contractor will be required to furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, and materials necessary to ensure safe, reliable, and compliant museum operations. The facility consists of an 84,000 sq. ft., six-story waterfront building situated on under 1 acre of grounds. Core requirements include, but are not limited to: HVAC & Environmental Controls: Continuous operation and maintenance of gas-fired condensing boilers, chillers, cooling towers, radiant flooring, and Building Automation Systems (BAS) to maintain strict gallery climate tolerances (68�F�72�F and 45%�55% Relative Humidity). Electrical, Plumbing, & Life Safety: Operations and maintenance of power distribution panels, emergency generators, fuel systems, fire alarms, fire extinguishers (NFPA 10), and water sprinkler systems (NFPA 25). Vertical Transportation: Monthly servicing, emergency response, and annual certified load testing for four (4) elevators. Custodial Services: A hybrid staffing model providing APPA Level 1 (Orderly Spotlessness) cleaning standards in high-traffic public galleries and APPA Level 4 in back-of-house staff areas. Grounds, Hardscape, & Snow Removal: Year-round exterior upkeep, power washing, and 24/7 bare-pavement snow and ice control (utilizing hardscape-safe compounds) for walkways, terraces, and flat roofing. Support Services: Integrated Pest Management (artifact-safe), catering kitchen equipment upkeep, and refuse/recycling stream management. Note: Museum artifacts, exhibit curation, and IT network infrastructure are excluded from this scope. See attachments for additional details

title: AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES STATISTICAL & CLINICAL COORDINATING CENTER (AD-SCCC)
description: Anticipated Period of Performance The anticipated period of performance is February 1, 2027 through January 31, 2028, with an option to extend services for an additional 6 month period, through July 31, 2028. Anticipated award date: February 1, 2027 The NAICS Code is 541715. Introduction The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) supports research related to the basic understanding of microbiology and immunology leading to the development of vaccines, therapeutics, and medical diagnostics for the prevention, treatment, and diagnosis of infectious and immune-mediated diseases. The NIAID, Division of Allergy, Immunology, and Transplantation (DAIT) has a requirement to support a broad range of services critical for the design, development, execution, and analysis of clinical research in autoimmune diseases. The major clinical research programs to be supported by this solicitation include, Autoimmunity Centers of Excellence and Immune Tolerance Network (ACE), as well as investigator initiated clinical trials (IICT), and other clinical trials or study activities supported by NIAID herein collectively referred to as NIAID supported research. Description Topic Title: Autoimmune Diseases Statistical & Clinical Coordinating Center (ADSCCC) The Division of Allergy, Immunology, and Transplantation (DAIT), National Institutes of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), project is for work related to the contract below: �Autoimmune Diseases Statistical & Clinical Coordinating Center (AD-SCCC)�, RHO Federal Systems Division, Inc. (Contract 75N93022C00003) This contract was awarded on a competitive basis for a five-year period from February 1, 2022 through January 31, 2027. A term type/level of effort contract was awarded for the delivery of 56,170 direct labor hours per year for Years 1-5. The total value of the contract is $49,268,667 and includes options for extension of the term for a total performance period of 5 years and options for increases in the level of effort, with the purpose of establishing an Autoimmune Diseases Statistical & Clinical Coordinating Center (AD- SCCC) that will provide a broad range of support critical for the design, development, execution, and analysis of clinical research sponsored by NIAID in autoimmune diseases and diseases related to mucosal immunology and primary immune deficiencies. The scope of clinical research to be supported by the AD- SCCC includes: (i) clinical trials at all phases to evaluate the safety and efficacy of investigational products and innovative approaches for disease treatment and prevention; (ii) studies of underlying mechanisms as integral components of clinical trials; (iii) clinical studies (e.g., genetic studies, microbiome studies, surveys of current therapies, etc.); and (iv) surrogate/biomarker studies. The scope of statistical and clinical support functions to be performed by the AD-SCCC includes statistical design and analysis; protocol development; study initiation and management; clinical safety and pharmacovigilance support; safety oversight; management of clinical study collaboration portals; manuscript preparation and management of sample repositories. The NIAID, NIH, conducts and supports basic and applied research to better understand, treat, and ultimately prevent infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases. The causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of autoimmune diseases are major areas of emphasis for NIAID�s Division of Allergy, Immunology, and Transplantation (DAIT). DAIT pursues research on autoimmune diseases by supporting investigator-initiated research projects, cooperative clinical studies, national networks of research centers, and demonstration and education research projects. A critical component of the Division�s mission focuses on clinical research to develop new and/or improved strategies to treat or prevent autoimmune diseases through rigorous evaluations of the safety and efficacy of investigational products and therapeutic interventions, studies to elucidate underlying mechanisms of disease, studies to develop and evaluate surrogate/biomarkers of disease stage, severity and progression, and clinical studies of disease natural history. The purpose of this acquisition is to extend the period of performance of the current contract (through July 31, 2028), beginning February 1, 2027, thereby maintaining the same direct labor hours to maintain ongoing clinical trial operations while DAIT completes the competition under the Clinical Data, Safety, and Coordinating Centers (CDSCC) NOFO. The extension retains the existing scope and contract type. The required research and development clinical trial activities are severable in nature, the 18-month extension will be structured as two discrete option periods. Specifically, the Contractor will be responsible for the following: A. Statistical Design Provide expertise, advice and assistance pin the development of statistical design plans for the development of concept and full study proposals for NIAID supported clinical research; Provide assistance in the preparation of concept and full proposals and study-specific protocols; Provide assistance in the preparation of concept and full proposals and protocols for mechanistic studies; Provide support for preclinical safety study evaluation by providing statistical expertise for, and participate in, evaluating the accuracy and validity of data from preclinical safety studies in support of clinical trials if applicable; Provide assistance for clinical trials and mechanistic studies post-study initiation. B. Statistical Analysis Development and preparation of the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for each clinical trial in conjunction with the Study Management Teams (SMTs); Preparation of interim and final analyses; Preparation of summary data reports; Development and preparation of results for posting as required by ClinicalTrials.gov; Review of the accuracy and completeness of statistical data and data analyses for all abstracts, manuscripts, and presentations reporting on the clinical studies conducted by the relevant NIAID-sponsored networks and investigators prior to presentation or submission for publication. Collaboration with NIAID-supported research, including the NIAID Clinical Data and Safety Management Center (CDSMC); C. Protocol Development and Study Initiation Provide expert advice and assistance to SMTs in the development of protocols for clinical trials and mechanistic studies; Provide expert advice, assistance and coordination in the preparation, writing, review and approval of protocol-related documents and materials in collaboration with NIAID, SMTs, and the CDSMC and other NIAID supported research. D. Data Management and Reporting E. Clinical Safety and Pharmacovigilance Center Support F. Safety Oversight Structure Support G. Clinical Study Internet-Based Collaboration Portals H. Training I. Repository of Biological Specimens J. Other Technical and Administrative Support K. Scientific and Technical Personnel L. Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources M. Quality Assurance/Quality Control N. Overall Project Management O. Initial and Final Transitions The NIAID intends to negotiate, under the authority of RFO - FAR Part 6.302-1 and HHSAR Part 306.302-1, on a sole source basis with Rho, to modify the existing contract to extend the current contract by a total of 18-months [Term Option 5 (12-months, February 1, 2027 through January 31, 2028), and Term Option 6 (6-months, February 1, 2028 through July 31, 2028)]. title: DLA Medical Equipment Electronic CATalog (ECAT) Generation V Program
description: Synopsis of Standing Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 DLA Troop Support, in an effort to improve medical supply support to our customers, developed the Electronic Catalog (ECAT) System. The ECAT System allows DLA Troop Support customers to review and compare contractor electronic catalogs with the ultimate goal of placing on-line orders to the contractor of their choice. Customers are currently using the ECAT System to order medical equipment and related supplies. Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 is a Request for Proposal (RFP) from which the Government will contemplate awards of contracts for Medical Equipment items as prescribed in the attached solicitation documents. This is the follow-on solicitation to our expired standing solicitation, SPE2DH-16-R-0002, which closed on August 15, 2021. This solicitation is a standing solicitation from which the Government contemplates award of contracts for medical equipment, accessories, and consumables. The solicitation will remain in effect five years from the issue date or when it is replaced by an updated solicitation, whichever comes first. Offerors are requested to submit complete proposals for all requirements, including all certifications, as specified in this solicitation. Proposals may be submitted at anytime during the open periods of the solicitation. DLA Troop Support intends to award multiple contracts to manufacturers, distributors and other specifically designated sources that support programs. The Government intends to award a contract to all responsible offerors who comply with the terms and conditions of the solicitation and whose prices are determined to be fair and reasonable. Any offeror that takes exception to any term or condition of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration for award. The items within scope of this solicitation are commercial medical equipment used by medical professionals, technicians, and laboratory personnel to perform a treatment, test, or operation, or to provide medical care for a patient. The scope of the solicitation also includes consumables and accessories for commercial medical equipment. Also included within the scope of the solicitation are medical simulation equipment used for training purposes. Please review solicitation pages 33-36 'Statement of Work' which outlines scope of products for consideration and product exclusions. The standing solicitation is also available via download from the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ . title: Air Force Civil Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: C222--589-27-108, Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Building 26 KCVA (ME) FY27 NRM VISN Base - AE (VA-27-00021035)
description: DESCRIPTION Project: 589-27-108 Solicitation Number: 36C25527Q0057 RFP: 36C25527R0018 Title: Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Type of Notice: Sources Sought Posted Date:11/16/2026 Response Date: 12/1/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: C222 -Architect and Engineering- Electrical Systems NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for SF330's or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the VA Medical Center located in Kansas City, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 541330 Engineering Services and the size standard is $25.5 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail to matthew.finley@va.gov and received no later than December 1, 2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Business Opportunities website https://www.fbo.gov once available. Period of Performance for all design work is 150 calendar days including time for VA reviews. Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-75, the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73. The prime architect shall provide written certification of this to the Contracting Officer with the response provided for this market research. GENERAL SCOPE OF DESIGN: The Architect/Engineer (A/E)) shall provide professional design services for a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, uninterruptible power, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center (KCVA), 4801 Linwood Blvd, Kansas City, MO 64128. A/E Part One Services (also known as the design phase) for this design project encompass site visits as needed, field investigations, and the conduct of studies and user interviews to prepare detailed drawings, specifications, and cost estimates. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate and provide construction period services for a construction project. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center. The A/E services are required for preparation of Narrative, Studies, Phasing Design, Schematic Designs, Design Development, Construction Documents, and As Built Documents. The A/E shall coordinate all disciplines necessary to deliver a complete electrical infrastructure project. The A/E shall not rely solely on record drawings and shall verify existing conditions before using them as the basis of design. Ensuring all required permits and licenses from federal, state/provincial, or local authorities are obtained for the construction, installation, and operation of the equipment is also part of the A/E s responsibilities. The project design will comply with Infection Control and Interim Life Safety Measures. The A/E will provide design drawing, specification, and IGCE submissions at 35% (Schematic Design), 65% (Design Development), 95% (Construction Documents), and Final Bid Documents for all disciplines necessary to complete the project to the VA. END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 541330 and qualified as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned small business under NAICS code 541330. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 541330. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this sources sought or Government use of any information provided. The Government will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any costs associated with submission of comments. There is no guarantee, expressed or implicit, that market research for this acquisition will result in a particular set-aside, or any other guarantee of award or acquisition strategy. Responses must be received by 2:00 PM Central on December 21, 2026 via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at Matthew.Finley@va.gov. PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: Project 589-27-108 Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26," IN THE SUBJECT LINE and cover sheet. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this Sources Sought notice. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://beta.sam.gov/. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. Contracting Office Address: Department of Veterans Affairs; Network 15 Contracting Office; 3450 S. 4th Street, Leavenworth, KS 66048 Point of Contact(s): Matt Finley, Contracting Officer, e-mail address: Matthew.Finley@va.gov

title: DLA Medical Equipment Electronic CATalog (ECAT) Generation V Program
description: Synopsis of Standing Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 DLA Troop Support, in an effort to improve medical supply support to our customers, developed the Electronic Catalog (ECAT) System. The ECAT System allows DLA Troop Support customers to review and compare contractor electronic catalogs with the ultimate goal of placing on-line orders to the contractor of their choice. Customers are currently using the ECAT System to order medical equipment and related supplies. Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 is a Request for Proposal (RFP) from which the Government will contemplate awards of contracts for Medical Equipment items as prescribed in the attached solicitation documents. This is the follow-on solicitation to our expired standing solicitation, SPE2DH-16-R-0002, which closed on August 15, 2021. This solicitation is a standing solicitation from which the Government contemplates award of contracts for medical equipment, accessories, and consumables. The solicitation will remain in effect five years from the issue date or when it is replaced by an updated solicitation, whichever comes first. Offerors are requested to submit complete proposals for all requirements, including all certifications, as specified in this solicitation. Proposals may be submitted at anytime during the open periods of the solicitation. DLA Troop Support intends to award multiple contracts to manufacturers, distributors and other specifically designated sources that support programs. The Government intends to award a contract to all responsible offerors who comply with the terms and conditions of the solicitation and whose prices are determined to be fair and reasonable. Any offeror that takes exception to any term or condition of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration for award. The items within scope of this solicitation are commercial medical equipment used by medical professionals, technicians, and laboratory personnel to perform a treatment, test, or operation, or to provide medical care for a patient. The scope of the solicitation also includes consumables and accessories for commercial medical equipment. Also included within the scope of the solicitation are medical simulation equipment used for training purposes. Please review solicitation pages 33-36 'Statement of Work' which outlines scope of products for consideration and product exclusions. The standing solicitation is also available via download from the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ . title: Helmet-Mounted First-Person View Display System
description: I. Description USSOCOM is conducting market research to identify sources capable of providing dismounted Special Operations Forces with a helmet-mounted first-person view (FPV) display. This display must deliver an expanded field of view, certified ballistic protection, real-time tactical information overlay, and unmanned system control in contested, congested, and all-weather environments. The effort aims to develop a 50-degree field-of-view Display Module that integrates full military ballistic protection, ATAK capability, head tracking, improved display performance, and expanded environmental durability while remaining compatible with existing soldier systems and helmets. This announcement is for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation. The Government will use responses to this notice to assess interest and capability within the industry and to determine the acquisition strategy (e.g., limited competition or small business set-aside). This Sources Sought is posted as a Call to Vulcan and all responses must be submitted to Vulcan. II. Requested Information Interested vendors are requested to submit the following information: Company Information: Company name, address, point of contact, CAGE code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CMMC/NIST (type, date, score), website. Business Size: Indicate your business size and socio-economic status (e.g., small business, 8(a), HUBZone, etc.). Confirm your business size relative to 541715 � Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). Security Clearance: Indicate your current facility clearance and the level of facility security clearances you can maintain. Relevant Experience: Provide a brief overview of your experience in supporting SOF, system testing, commercial integration, and ATAK areas as listed below. If no experience, briefly identify the names and CAGE codes of any small businesses that have demonstrated experience that your company can team/partner with on this requirement. Display Systems. System testing (researching, planning, designing, developing, analyzing, and testing a variety of electronic equipment and systems, military command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C5ISR) systems, interface units, and other electronic devices and test equipment) to support enhanced situational awareness, command and control, and precision effects while retaining mobility, protection, and compatibility with existing soldier equipment. Experience with existing soldier equipment (ATAK EUD, radios, hubs). Experience with researching, testing, and integrating emerging technologies as they pertain to real-time overlay of ATAK tactical data, targeting information, and UAS video/control in day, night, and all-weather contested environments. Capability Statement: Submit a capability statement that responds to the following questions: Describe your company�s relevant experience providing SOF support in any of the following areas: ATAK interface, ballistic protection integration, development testing, head tracking sensor integration, software updates and integration, integrating processing hardware and the Display Module into a single module, Windblast compatibility, Expanded environmental envelope, similar requirements or related mission sets. Include contract numbers, customers, and scope. Explain your approach to development milestones (SRR, PDR, CDR, development tests, prototype deliveries) for the combined work scope versus individual items and identify any related any similar efforts. Confirm your company�s ability to maintain adherence to milestones and react to shifts within technology or supply chains to avoid impact to development and enable future scaling of production. Describe your recruiting, screening, and retention strategy for specialized Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). Explain how your company would manage and execute a contract for this development. What program management tools, structures, or practices will ensure successful delivery? Describe your Quality Assurance/Quality Control processes and how they would ensure compliance with the Statement of Objectives (SOO), Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) and Key System Attributes (KSAs). If applicable, identify any suppliers, subcontractors or teaming partners. Specify their roles and the percentage of work they are expected to perform. Identify any services within the SOO that meet the definition of commercial services under FAR 2.101. Provide catalog pricing or related contract references. Provide feedback on a recommendation on contract type and structure (length, phases, single award, FFP/CPFF, OTA). Are there any risks or constraints that may affect your participation? Identify how the USSOCOM can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. Identify any condition or action that may be having the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion. Recommendations to improve the approach/specifications/NAICS/PSC/ DRAFT SOO to acquiring the identified items/services. III. Submission Details Submission Deadline: 3:00 Eastern on 01-DEC-2026 Submission Location: All submissions shall be made within https://vulcan-sof.com/ Submit To: https://vulcan-sof.com/login/ng2/submission?collectionUuid=a26a99ef-c351-464f-af93-dbcc064df521 IV. Disclaimer This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal. Responses will not be returned, and the Government will not reimburse costs incurred in response preparation. Participation in this notice is not a guarantee of future contract award.

title: DLA Medical Equipment Electronic CATalog (ECAT) Generation V Program
description: Synopsis of Standing Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 DLA Troop Support, in an effort to improve medical supply support to our customers, developed the Electronic Catalog (ECAT) System. The ECAT System allows DLA Troop Support customers to review and compare contractor electronic catalogs with the ultimate goal of placing on-line orders to the contractor of their choice. Customers are currently using the ECAT System to order medical equipment and related supplies. Solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 is a Request for Proposal (RFP) from which the Government will contemplate awards of contracts for Medical Equipment items as prescribed in the attached solicitation documents. This is the follow-on solicitation to our expired standing solicitation, SPE2DH-16-R-0002, which closed on August 15, 2021. This solicitation is a standing solicitation from which the Government contemplates award of contracts for medical equipment, accessories, and consumables. The solicitation will remain in effect five years from the issue date or when it is replaced by an updated solicitation, whichever comes first. Offerors are requested to submit complete proposals for all requirements, including all certifications, as specified in this solicitation. Proposals may be submitted at anytime during the open periods of the solicitation. DLA Troop Support intends to award multiple contracts to manufacturers, distributors and other specifically designated sources that support programs. The Government intends to award a contract to all responsible offerors who comply with the terms and conditions of the solicitation and whose prices are determined to be fair and reasonable. Any offeror that takes exception to any term or condition of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration for award. The items within scope of this solicitation are commercial medical equipment used by medical professionals, technicians, and laboratory personnel to perform a treatment, test, or operation, or to provide medical care for a patient. The scope of the solicitation also includes consumables and accessories for commercial medical equipment. Also included within the scope of the solicitation are medical simulation equipment used for training purposes. Please review solicitation pages 33-36 'Statement of Work' which outlines scope of products for consideration and product exclusions. The standing solicitation is also available via download from the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ . Amendment 0001 issued against solicitation SPE2DH21R0002- 30 NOV 2022.

title: Preventive Maintenance and Repair Services - Kahuku Training Area (KTA)
description: The Regional Contracting Office Hawaii (RCO-HI) has a requirement for preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, unscheduled assessment/trouble-call, and repair services for HVAC; fire alarm and mass notification; emergency lighting and exit signs; and lightning protection systems at Kahuku Training Area, Oahu, Hawaii. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, supervision, and other resources necessary to perform the requirement in accordance with the solicitation and Performance Work Statement. This solicitation is issued as Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. W912CN27QA008 and is a 100 percent Total Small Business Set-Aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 561210. The Government contemplates award of one firm-fixed-price requirements contract consisting of a base period and four 12-month option periods, with evaluation of the six-month option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation is conducted under the provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. To be eligible for award, quoters must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), including current and complete representations and certifications, at the time of quote submission and at the time of award. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and other solicitation information through the closing date. Refer to Section L, pages 113�116, for quote-submission instructions and required submission content, and Section M, pages 120�121, for evaluation criteria. Quoters must submit all required documents, including the signed SF 1449 and acknowledgement of all amendments, completed pricing documents for all applicable priced CLINs, and the technical capability submission. Do not price Repair Services CLIN 0006 or its option-year counterparts; repair services will be ordered and priced after award through Contracting Officer-issued firm-fixed-price task orders. Written questions are due no later than 10:00 a.m. Hawaii Standard Time (HST), Thursday, 12 November 2026. Questions shall be submitted to both: Travis Tonini, Contract Specialist: travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil Keely K. Pool, Contracting Officer: keely.k.pool.civ@army.mil Completed quotations and all supporting documentation must be submitted electronically by email to Travis Tonini at travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil no later than 10:00 a.m. HST, Tuesday, 1 December 2026. Faxed quotations will not be accepted. A site visit at Kahuku Training Area is scheduled for Tuesday, 10 November 2026. Attendance is strongly encouraged but not mandatory. Offerors intending to attend must submit required visit-request information no later than 12:00 p.m. HST, Friday, 6 November 2026, to Travis Tonini for further instructions.

title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract
description: Title: SIOP MMDD MACC. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) has a requirement to provide predominantly construction services (design build (DB) and design-bid-build (DBB)) for heavy and civil engineering waterfront facilities as well as commercial and institutional facilities primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock (MMDD) at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of NAVFAC Pacific. This solicitation will result in the award of Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC). The period of performance will be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. Each MACC holder will receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. This solicitation is unrestricted allowing for full and open competition. Large businesses are advised that an acceptable small business subcontracting plan is required. Primary North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M.Secondary NAICS code 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; Small Business Size Standard: $45M. Amendment 0001- Issued 21 October 2026. Amendment 0002- Issued 28 October 2026. Refer to the link to the PIEE Solicitation Module for all solicitation documents, attachments, amendments, and related details.

title: C222--589-27-108, Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Building 26 KCVA (ME) FY27 NRM VISN Base - AE (VA-27-00021035)
description: DESCRIPTION Project: 589-27-108 Solicitation Number: 36C25527Q0057 RFP: 36C25527R0018 Title: Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Type of Notice: Sources Sought Posted Date:11/16/2026 Response Date: 12/1/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: C222 -Architect and Engineering- Electrical Systems NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for SF330's or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the VA Medical Center located in Kansas City, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 541330 Engineering Services and the size standard is $25.5 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail to matthew.finley@va.gov and received no later than December 1, 2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Business Opportunities website https://www.fbo.gov once available. Period of Performance for all design work is 150 calendar days including time for VA reviews. Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-75, the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73. The prime architect shall provide written certification of this to the Contracting Officer with the response provided for this market research. GENERAL SCOPE OF DESIGN: The Architect/Engineer (A/E)) shall provide professional design services for a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, uninterruptible power, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center (KCVA), 4801 Linwood Blvd, Kansas City, MO 64128. A/E Part One Services (also known as the design phase) for this design project encompass site visits as needed, field investigations, and the conduct of studies and user interviews to prepare detailed drawings, specifications, and cost estimates. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate and provide construction period services for a construction project. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center. The A/E services are required for preparation of Narrative, Studies, Phasing Design, Schematic Designs, Design Development, Construction Documents, and As Built Documents. The A/E shall coordinate all disciplines necessary to deliver a complete electrical infrastructure project. The A/E shall not rely solely on record drawings and shall verify existing conditions before using them as the basis of design. Ensuring all required permits and licenses from federal, state/provincial, or local authorities are obtained for the construction, installation, and operation of the equipment is also part of the A/E s responsibilities. The project design will comply with Infection Control and Interim Life Safety Measures. The A/E will provide design drawing, specification, and IGCE submissions at 35% (Schematic Design), 65% (Design Development), 95% (Construction Documents), and Final Bid Documents for all disciplines necessary to complete the project to the VA. END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 541330 and qualified as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned small business under NAICS code 541330. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 541330. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this sources sought or Government use of any information provided. The Government will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any costs associated with submission of comments. There is no guarantee, expressed or implicit, that market research for this acquisition will result in a particular set-aside, or any other guarantee of award or acquisition strategy. Responses must be received by 2:00 PM Central on December 21, 2026 via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at Matthew.Finley@va.gov. PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: Project 589-27-108 Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26," IN THE SUBJECT LINE and cover sheet. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this Sources Sought notice. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://beta.sam.gov/. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. Contracting Office Address: Department of Veterans Affairs; Network 15 Contracting Office; 3450 S. 4th Street, Leavenworth, KS 66048 Point of Contact(s): Matt Finley, Contracting Officer, e-mail address: Matthew.Finley@va.gov

title: KC-130J � In-Flight Refueling Aircraft Parts & Equipment
description: 1 PROGRAM BACKGROUND: This sources sought is issued by the Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD. The U.S. Marine Corp (USMC) and U.S. Navy Reserves (USNR) Tactical Air Lift Program (KC-130J Aircraft) PMA-207 is conducting a market survey of industry to determine potential interested sources that can provide In-Flight Refueling (IFR) aircraft pods, pods parts, fuse tank parts and equipment manufacturing; associated equipment including spares, repair parts, support equipment, technical manuals, training; and logistical engineering and field technical support. This market research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible vendors of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. Responses will also be utilized by the Government for market research purposes in developing its acquisition/contracting strategy. All interested parties must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) government website at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of Government contracts. This sources sought is used as a market research tool pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 10 to determine potential sources and their technical capabilities. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code currently assigned to this procurement is 336413 � Aircraft Auxiliary Parts. The product service code (PSC) is 1680 - Miscellaneous Aircraft Accessories and Components. In-Flight Refueling parts/equipment is currently employed on USMC and USNR C-130 aircraft and meets System Performance Specifications for the KC-130J Tanker Aircraft, Model 382U-UUS-93, dated 23 March 2012. title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract
description: Title: SIOP MMDD MACCThe Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) has a requirement to provide predominantly construction services (design build (DB) and design-bid-build (DBB)) for heavy and civil engineering waterfront facilities as well as commercial and institutional facilities primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock (MMDD) at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of NAVFAC Pacific. This solicitation will result in the award of Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC). The period of performance will be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. Each MACC holder will receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. This solicitation is unrestricted allowing for full and open competition. Large businesses are advised that an acceptable small business subcontracting plan is required. title: C222--589-27-108, Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Building 26 KCVA (ME) FY27 NRM VISN Base - AE (VA-27-00021035)
description: DESCRIPTION Project: 589-27-108 Solicitation Number: 36C25527Q0057 RFP: 36C25527R0018 Title: Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Type of Notice: Sources Sought Posted Date:11/16/2026 Response Date: 12/1/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: C222 -Architect and Engineering- Electrical Systems NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for SF330's or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the VA Medical Center located in Kansas City, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 541330 Engineering Services and the size standard is $25.5 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail to matthew.finley@va.gov and received no later than December 1, 2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Business Opportunities website https://www.fbo.gov once available. Period of Performance for all design work is 150 calendar days including time for VA reviews. Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-75, the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73. The prime architect shall provide written certification of this to the Contracting Officer with the response provided for this market research. GENERAL SCOPE OF DESIGN: The Architect/Engineer (A/E)) shall provide professional design services for a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, uninterruptible power, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center (KCVA), 4801 Linwood Blvd, Kansas City, MO 64128. A/E Part One Services (also known as the design phase) for this design project encompass site visits as needed, field investigations, and the conduct of studies and user interviews to prepare detailed drawings, specifications, and cost estimates. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate and provide construction period services for a construction project. This effort covers all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a complete, coordinated, constructible, and independently usable project to correct electrical closets, secondary distribution, and emergency power deficiencies in Building 26 at the Kansas City VA Medical Center. The A/E services are required for preparation of Narrative, Studies, Phasing Design, Schematic Designs, Design Development, Construction Documents, and As Built Documents. The A/E shall coordinate all disciplines necessary to deliver a complete electrical infrastructure project. The A/E shall not rely solely on record drawings and shall verify existing conditions before using them as the basis of design. Ensuring all required permits and licenses from federal, state/provincial, or local authorities are obtained for the construction, installation, and operation of the equipment is also part of the A/E s responsibilities. The project design will comply with Infection Control and Interim Life Safety Measures. The A/E will provide design drawing, specification, and IGCE submissions at 35% (Schematic Design), 65% (Design Development), 95% (Construction Documents), and Final Bid Documents for all disciplines necessary to complete the project to the VA. END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 541330 and qualified as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned small business under NAICS code 541330. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 541330. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this sources sought or Government use of any information provided. The Government will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any costs associated with submission of comments. There is no guarantee, expressed or implicit, that market research for this acquisition will result in a particular set-aside, or any other guarantee of award or acquisition strategy. Responses must be received by 2:00 PM Central on December 21, 2026 via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at Matthew.Finley@va.gov. PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: Project 589-27-108 Correct Electrical Deficiencies in Bldg. 26," IN THE SUBJECT LINE and cover sheet. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this Sources Sought notice. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://beta.sam.gov/. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. Contracting Office Address: Department of Veterans Affairs; Network 15 Contracting Office; 3450 S. 4th Street, Leavenworth, KS 66048 Point of Contact(s): Matt Finley, Contracting Officer, e-mail address: Matthew.Finley@va.gov

title: Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler, St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1284LL27Q0008 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler. Services and supplies are required for the currently installed tree cooler for the St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The tree cooler was built in 1984, the outdated HVAC system shall be replaced with a new HVAC system. The contractor shall provide a fully functioning new HVAC system for the existing tree cooler with associated evaporator fans and necessary materials for the refrigeration system. Contractor shall remove any humidifiers and associated parts, update the lighting, and install a notification system of a power outage due to ongoing power fluctuations. The contractor shall provide the personnel, materials, and equipment needed to perform the required services to industry standards and specifications. Representative shall communicate with POC regarding any issues that may arise. Contractor shall coordinate work hours with CO and COR for site access, hours, and operation. There will be no Government Property issued. Electricity will be available on site for Contractor's use. All work shall be completed by 03/15/2027. See attachment 1284LL27Q0008 for more details. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 811310 The small business size standard is $12.5 million dollars. title: Interactive Electronic Technical Manual LiveContent Viewer License
description: The United States Air Force (USAF) and Headquarters Air Mobility Command (HQ AMC) A4 established the requirement that all C-17 aircraft technical manuals (TM) will use the S1000D Specification Issue 4.0.2 or later versions of the technical data specification. Where cost-effective, the S1000D Issue 4.0.2 or later version will also be used to transform existing aircraft technical data to Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETM) Type Two format. The contractor shall maintain the authorized perpetual FMS LiveContent S1000D Standalone Consumer License � Per Land, Sea or Air Vehicle for the 29 C-17 aircraft. Annual maintenance support for all perpetual licenses shall be made available for a total of five years. An initial year shall be provided at contract award, with 4 additional one-year options. The total period of performance will be five years after contract award. The contractor shall provide five years of support services to assist in any technical difficulties that may arise and update the software via software updates, patches, or minor and major releases of new software at no additional cost to the customer. Initial support will be provided by TOMA personnel but any technical problems that cannot be remedied will be referred to RWS for corrective action.

title: CAPACITY ON A UHF-CAPABLE ON-ORBIT MEO SATELLITE
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to bandwidth carried by a commercially owned, commercially operated UHF-capable on-orbit MEO satellite for use in a near-term experimental campaign to: Characterize spectrum, waveform, and user equipment operation with a MEO UHF system Demonstrate interoperability between a potential future MEO UHF system and the existing GEO constellation Inform a time-sequenced pathway to augment or replace the GEO UHF system with a MEO capability The offeror should consider technology solutions that prioritize existing space vehicle, payload and communications link capabilities to provide on-orbit service immediately or as soon as possible. An Initial Launch Capability (ILC) by 2030 is potentially useful, but innovative approaches leading to earlier on-orbit capability are strongly desired. The Government recognizes that this initial prototype may not be fully representative of a final, future architecture, but rather represents an initial step to explore providing UHF services from MEO. AMENDMENT 1 (23 Jul 2026) The following changes are hereby made to the above announcement: Corrects the uplink and downlink frequency bands in Section 4.0.a.i The attachment entitled "pMEO Demo Request for Information_FINAL 10 Jul 26" is removed in its entirety and replaced with "pMEO Demo Request for Information_AMEND1 23 Jul 26". All other RFI content and due dates remain unchanged. Refer to the attachment entitled "pMEO Demo Request for Information_AMEND1 23 Jul 26" for full details.

title: Intent to Sole Source - Dredge Donnelly Operation Simulator
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT Notice ID: PANNAD-26-P-0000 032679/ W912BU-27-Q-A003 Department/Agency: USACE Philadelphia District Product Service Code (PSC): 6930 � Operation Training Devices NAICS Code: 333310 � Commercial and Service Industry Machinery Manufacturing Introduction and Background This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with RFO 5.101. This Notice does NOT constitute a request for competitive proposals, bids or quotes. The USACE Philadelphia District intends to award a contract on a noncompetitive basis under the authority of RFO 6.103-1(d) ("Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements"). Intended Awardee: IHC SMIT B.V. UEI: SZYEPF3FD2J1 CAGE Code: H2SY5 Address: Smitweg 6 , Kinderdijk 2961AW , Netherlands 2. Authority The proposed procurement is justified under the authority of 10 USC �3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1(d). This authority is applicable because RFO 6.103-1(d) allows for specification of attributes peculiar to one manufacturer in which the Dredge Donnelly Vessel Simulator is a product which requires the specification of attributes peculiar to one manufacturer: the designer of the Dredge DONNNELLY. 3. Description of Agency Requirement The supply to be furnished under this contract action is a custom hopper Dredge DONNELLY operating simulator that exactly mimics the actual controls and operation of the USACE hopper dredge DONNELLY. This procurement is necessary to fulfill the mission of the Dredge DONNELLY because the simulator will be used to train the DONNELLY crew. The simulator reacts in the same way the actual dredge would but in a simulated classroom style environment on multiple displays that match the view an operator would get if in the actual vessel�s pilothouse. The simulator must be developed based upon the actual layout of the controls on Dredge DONNELLY and actual functional response of those controls, as well as responses from sensors and alarms. External inputs to include specific geographic conditions, specific dredging conditions, and variable environmental and dredging conditions and parameters will be simulated. The simulator is a custom manufactured system utilizing the background design data from the hopper dredge itself, including the custom physical operator�s chair, which has control and monitoring capability built into it. In summary, the dredge simulator must exactly mimic the Dredge DONNELLY controls; these attributes are peculiar to one manufacturer: the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY. No other source has that information. 4. Justification for Sole Source IHC SMIT B.V. is the only responsible source to provide this dredge simulator and no other source will satisfy the Agency�s requirement because the specifications of the simulator require information and attributes that are particular and peculiar to only Royal IHC as the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY as set forth at RFO 6.103-1(d). As explained above, the simulator will be developed to exactly match the dredge operator�s station on the Dredge DONNELLY and exactly replicate the actual movements of the dredge based on the operator�s use of the simulator. IHC SMIT B.V.is the only company that has all of the information necessary to build a working functional simulator of the Dredge DONNELLY. That information includes, but is not limited to, the following: It has all the design background information related to this dredge; not only the physical layout, but all the engineering that has been produced and utilized in the background to include how the dredge will respond to various commands and how the dredge will display various alarms and malfunctions. It knows how all the vessel dredging components work, and how they interact. It knows the ranges of all the operating features and projected vessel reactions and performance. It has an extensive library of vessel operating parameters that can be altered to allow operators to change conditions in the simulation. It has the capability to integrate vessel operating simulation with geographical background simulation. As noted above, the simulator cannot be completed until the actual dredge itself goes through commissioning and all operational systems are finalized because they must match exactly. This reinforces why Royal IHC is the only responsible source who can produce the dredge simulator. In summary, the simulator requires specification of attributes peculiar to one manufacturer: the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY. This prevents full and open competition. No other source has access to the information required to produce the simulator. 5. Market Research Discussions were held with UASCE employee who manages the simulation laboratory at ERDC � USACE. Those discussions confirmed that the use of proprietary information running in the software for this simulator as well as the custom design of the operator�s station that exactly matches the station on the actual dredge make it impossible for anyone else to build the simulator specific to this application. It also builds in the exact operation of the dredge navigation and automation performance. While there are many organizations that can create simulators, they are all customized to specific operation being simulated and require the actual engineering of that operation and the items configuration and operating environment. Simple simulators display generic performance, but sophisticated simulators mimic the exact operation of the operation being simulated. They indicated that ERDC builds simulations for channel design based on general vessel performance input (turning radius, draft vessel size, etc.) Since channel design is their area of expertise, they have the background information needed and can design simulations for channel design. Keith reinforced that there are firms that could generate simulation software, but that without the background technical information and the specifics needed in this application, any simulation produced by others would include significant guesswork and only be of very limited value. 6. Conclusion IHC SMIT B.V. is the only responsible source to provide this dredge simulator and no other source will satisfy the Agency�s requirement because the specifications of the simulator require information and attributes that are particular and peculiar to only IHC SMIT B.V. as the designer of the Dredge DONNELLY as set forth at RFO 6.103-1(d). As explained above, the simulator will be developed to exactly match the dredge operator�s station on the Dredge DONNELLY and exactly replicate the actual movements of the dredge based on the operator�s use of the simulator..
