title: Request for Information (RFI): Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) Project
description: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources for sun/sky/lunar scanning photometers and replacement parts in support of the Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) in the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. AERONET is a global network of ground-based sun and sky-scanning radiometers that measures aerosol optical properties and precipitable water in near real time. NASA uses AERONET data to validate satellite aerosol retrievals and to maintain a uniform long-term record of aerosol properties. AERONET's installed base is more than 600 CE318-series photometers at land, ocean, and ship sites worldwide. The value of the network depends on standardized measurement, calibration, data format, and processing across every site. Any instrument added to the network must produce data that can be merged into the AERONET record and must work with the network's existing site infrastructure, including its tracking robots. The Government requires a contractor to supply both new sun/sky/lunar scanning photometers and replacement parts for the fielded fleet. New instruments are required in standard, polarization, and ocean-color configurations. They must automatically measure direct sun and lunar irradiance and diffuse sky radiance from 340 to 1640 nm; achieve a signal-to-noise ratio above 10,000:1 on all channels; transmit data through the NOAA/NESDIS Data Collection System (DCS), worldwide 4G/5G cellular networks, and PC/internet; run unattended on battery and 5-watt solar power; and operate sealed against rain, humidity, dust, and smoke from -20 to 50 degrees C. Replacement parts, such as sensor head cards, detectors, filters, collimators, CPU cards, modems, robot hardware, and gear reducer motor assemblies, must fit and work in NASA's fielded CE318-series instruments. NASA/GSFC is seeking capability statements from U.S. VENDORS ONLY, for the purposes of determining the appropriate acquisition strategy and level of competition for this requirement. For this RFI, a U.S. vendor is a firm organized under the laws of the United States or a U.S. state, with its principal place of business in the United States. NASA welcomes responses from U.S. manufacturers, authorized U.S. distributors, and other U.S. firms, including all socioeconomic categories of small business. Capability statements from foreign firms will not be reviewed. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small, 8(a), Women-owned (WOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women-owned Small Business (EDWOSB), or HUBZone business set-aside based on responses received. Interested firms that possess the capability to meet the above requirement as described in the attached Statement of Work (SOW) are encouraged to submit a capability statement indicating the ability to meet all aspects of the requirement. NASA seeks input in the following areas: 1. Whether your firm is the manufacturer, an authorized distributor, or a reseller. Identify the manufacturer and country of manufacture for each item you would supply. 2. How your instruments meet the measurement, performance, communication, power, and environmental requirements in the SOW. If your instrument is not a CE318-series unit, explain how it would produce data compatible with the AERONET record, for example through side-by-side intercalibration results or use in AERONET or a similar federated network. 3. How your firm would supply replacement parts that fit and work in the fielded CE318-series units. 4. Your firm's experience supplying similar instruments or parts to government, research, or commercial customers in the past five years, with contract numbers and customer contacts. 5. Whether the items are commercial products as defined in FAR 2.101, and any applicable GSA Schedule or other government-wide contract vehicle. 6. Any requirement in the SOW that you believe unnecessarily limits competition, and what you would recommend instead. Each capability statement should also include the firm's name, address, Unique Entity ID (UEI), CAGE code, SAM.gov registration status, business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 334516, and a point of contact with name, title, phone, and email. All capability statements and RFI responses shall be submitted electronically via email to Contract Specialist Kermit Stanbach at kermit.s.stanbach@nasa.gov and Contracting Officer Cassandra Moore at cassandra.k.moore@nasa.gov no later than December 1, 2026, 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. Please reference Notice ID 80GSFC27Q0008 in any response. NASA intends to publicize a listing of respondents in order to facilitate teaming arrangements. Should your firm desire not to be included in this listing, clearly indicate this desire in your response.

description: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. This existing condition produces flooding and sediment deposition, which creates unsafe conditions for visitors, triggers road closures, potentially strands Park visitors, diminishes visitor experience of the Park, and generates high operational costs associated with traffic management, visitor safety, and cleanup operations. SCOPE OF THE WORK: This project will be designated as Reconstruction (4R) with one segment of restoration (3R), and will design and construct 100� span concrete bridges at the Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash. The DA roadway profile at each Wash will be raised to accommodate a 10-year design frequency and allow a medium-sized excavator to access each wash. The DA will be realigned at the Salt Valley wash, moving the roadway and new bridge location to the north of the existing roadway and drainage crossing. The remaining 3R sections of the roadway will receive full depth reclamation (FDR) or removal of pavement, including all parking areas, followed by a 4-inch pavement overlay. title: J046--Water Tank Inspection & Disinfection
description: The Malcolm Randall VA Medical Center requires a one-time internal and external inspection of its 750,000-gallon water tower to satisfy the required five-year inspection cycle. Contractors are strongly encouraged to attend the site visit to evaluate site conditions and determine the resources, equipment, and personnel necessary to fulfill all requirements of this Statement of Work. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision, and incidentals necessary to perform a one-time five-year internal and external inspection, Water Tower Evaluation and Report, and Water Tower Washout and Disinfection in accordance with AWWA C652-11 for the 750,000-gallon water tower located at the Malcolm Randall VA Medical Center, 1601 SW Archer Road, Gainesville, FL 32608. All services shall be performed in accordance with the requirements of this Statement of Work.

title: Request For Proposal (RFP) for NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium
description: Update 11/13/2026 The purpose of this announcement is to publish Amendment 0003 to Solicitation 80KSC024R0010 for the 2027 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In (Amendment 0001 and Amendment 0002 were posted with the origninal solicitation), extend the proposal due date from November 20, 2026, to December 1, 2026, and provide Questions and Answers. See attached 80KSC024R0010 Amendment 0003 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In and 80KSC024R0010 2027 IDIQ CLIN Opt-In Questions and Answers. ____________________________________________________________________ UPDATE 10/20/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Supply of Liquid and Gaseous Helium opt-in opportunity as described in the original Helium Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.10, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium RFP was issued on December 21, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2.10.1, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The Helium contract's ordering period remains valid through September 30, 2030. The RFP has resulted in the award of four fixed-price indefinite delivery (ID) requirements contracts to supply liquid and gaseous helium in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. Awards were made to the following companies: Airgas USA LLC (South), Airgas USA LLC (West), Linde, Inc., and Messer LLC. Each year during the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from new entrants for each IDIQ subCLIN location and the Government will also accept proposals from existing helium contractors for each additional IDIQ subCLIN location. A new entrant is a company that does not currently hold a NASA liquid and gaseous helium contract. The Government will evaluate the proposals to determine technical acceptability for a specific NASA location. Upon the Government's determination of technical acceptability, a contract (for new entrants) or contract modification (for existing helium Contractors) will be executed to add the Contractor to the IDIQ CLIN Pool for the specific NASA location. Thereafter, the Contractor will be eligible to participate in the IDIQ CLIN Pool process described in Section 2.10 for the NASA locations awarded to that Contractor. All eligible Contractors who are awarded an IDIQ subCLIN for a particular NASA location will have the option to compete for requirements within those IDIQ subCLINs which they are awarded. The commodities will support current and future aerospace flight, simulation, research, development, testing, and other operations at the following NASA centers and facilities: Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility (CSBF) locations (Palestine, TX, Ft Sumner, NM, Port Hueneme, CA, and Burns, OR); Glenn Research Center (GRC), Cleveland, OH 44135; GRC Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (GRC-ATF), Sandusky, OH 44870; Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Greenbelt, MD 20771; Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Pasadena, CA 91109; Johnson Space Center (JSC), Houston, TX 77058; Kennedy Space Center (KSC - including Cape Canaveral Space Force Station - CCSFS); Langley Research Center (LaRC), Hampton, VA 23666; Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, AL, 35812; Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF), New Orleans, LA 70129; Stennis Space Center (SSC), Stennis Space Center, MS, 39529; White Sands Test Facility (WSTF), Las Cruces, NM 88012; and other such places of performance as required in this contract. Submission information: 1. Opt-in by a Current Helium Contractor. A current Helium Contractor shall submit Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. If the Contractor is determined technically acceptable, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). 2. Opt-in by New Entrant. The new entrant shall submit an Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in contract Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Gaseous and Liquid Helium - Requirements. Once determined acceptable from a technical standpoint, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). New entrants will be required to comply with provisions in Section 5 of the RFP and all terms and conditions of the resulting contract. 3. All questions regarding this opt-in notice shall be submitted in writing via email to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. The Government will not answer oral questions due to the possibility of misunderstanding or misinterpretation. The Offeror shall submit all questions, if any, no later than November 4, 2026, to allow for analysis and dissemination of responses in advance of the proposal due date. The Government will not guarantee a response to late questions. Questions shall not be directed to the technical activity personnel. 4. It is requested that any interested party notify the helium Contracting Officers via email no later than November 4, 2026, of your intent to submit a proposal during this opt-in period as well as the name(s) of which NASA Center(s) you intend to propose. Please send your notice of intent to propose to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov. 5. All offers shall be sent to Hillary Heard at hillary.p.heard@nasa.gov, and Shana Thompson at shana.d.thompson@nasa.gov by November 20, 2026, by 4:30PM EST. Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, paragraph (f). 6. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition is Marcus Orr, Acting Deputy Procurement Officer at marcus.c.orr@nasa.gov. ************************************** Amendment 0002. buyer: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH (HZB)
title: Germany – Laboratory furniture – V456_2026 - HiPOLE - Laborausstattung inkl. Planung (Lab2Fab)
description: Als eines von 18 Zentren der Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft beschäftigt das Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie (HZB) rund 1.400 Mitarbeiter an den Standorten Berlin-Wannsee und Berlin-Adlershof – und verfügt über einen Gesamthaushalt von zirka 110 Millionen Euro. Das HZB arbeitet eng mit den Universitäten und Fachhochschulen in Berlin-Brandenburg zusammen. Das HZB forscht an Lösungen für eine klimaneutrale Gesellschaft. Forschende entwickeln und optimieren effiziente und preiswerte Materialien für Solarzellen, Batterien und Katalysatoren. Diese Energiematerialien sind wesentliche Bausteine auf dem Weg in eine CO2-neutrale und sichere Energieversorgung. Wichtigstes Werkzeug ist die Röntgenquelle BESSY II, welche intensives Licht im weichen Röntgenbereich liefert. Damit wird der Aufbau von Energie- und Quantenmaterialien sowie ihre Funktionsweise untersucht. Das HZB forscht auch an neuen Konzepten für beschleunigerbasierte Röntgenquellen und entwickelt neue Instrumente mit immer höheren Messgenauigkeiten. Das HZB und die Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena gründeten 2023 das Helmholtz-Institut für Polymere in Energieanwendungen (HIPOLE) in Jena als dauerhafte Einrichtung des HZB. Führende Expertisen in den Bereichen Energiespeicherung und Photovoltaik, polymere Materialien, künstliche Intelligenz sowie nachhaltige Chemie konnten somit gebündelt werden, um die beschleunigte wissensbasierte Erforschung nachhaltiger Polymermaterialien für skalierbare Energietechnologien voranzubringen. HIPOLE Jena basiert auf drei Forschungssäulen: • Materialdesign und Synthese • Skalierbarkeit, Prototypen und Transfer sowie • Charakterisierung, Theorie, Modellierung und Datenwissenschaften. Der Fokus liegt nicht nur in der Grundlagenforschung, sondern auch im Transfer der Forschungsergebnisse. Aktuell sind an HIPOLE Jena rund 50 Mitarbeitende beschäftigt. Die Forschungsarbeiten der Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler am HIPOLE Jena, unterstützt von sieben assoziierten Mitgliedern der FSU Jena und des HZB, lassen sich fünf Forschungsbereichen zuordnen: 1. Polymere Redox-Flow Batterien, 2. Polymer-basierte Dünnschichtbatterien, 3. Photovoltaik, 4. Funktionale selbstheilende Materialien und 5. Nachhaltige Chemie. Das Helmholtz-Institut für Polymere in Energieanwendungen Jena (HIPOLE Jena) beabsichtigt die Beschaffung von Laborausstattung inkl. Planung (Lab2Fab). Es sollen drei Laborräume mit Labormöbeln in bezugsfertigen Laborflächen im Lab2Fab in Jena ausgestattet werden.

Atlikti projektinius inžinerinius geologinius ir geotechninius tyrimus, gauti jų ataskaitą su tyrimų registravimo numeriu Žemės gelmių registre ir Lietuvos geologijos tarnybos rašto apie šios ataskaitos vertinimą ir priėmimą kopiją; gauti žemės valdytojų sutikimus (esant poreikiui); ●Parengti/papildyti topografinių tyrinėjimų ataskaitą (topografinio plano ir inžinerinių tinklų plano sudarymas) su esamų medžių taksacija; ●Parengti želdinių (medžių) vertinimo ataskaitą ● Atlikti želdynų ekspertizę. ●Gauti specialiuosius reikalavimus ir prisijungimo sąlygas;●Organizuoti Kūrybines dirbtuves; Tarpinstitucinius susitikimus (TRSA, KPD); ● Organizuoti ir atlikti visus Sutartyje ir Techninėje projektavimo užduotyje numatytus darbus; ●Parengti, suderinti su Užsakovu bei jam perduoti Užsakovo planuojamo statyti Statinio pilnos sudėties projektą (toliau – Projektas). ● Gavus bendrosios, specialiosios ekspertizės ir derinimo IS Infostatyba institucijų pastabas atsižvelgti ir taisyti sprendinius. ● Veikiant Užsakovo vardu paslaugų teikėjas gauna statybą leidžiantį dokumentą ir visus kitus suderinimus, patvirtinimus ir leidimus, reikalingus Techninio darbo projekto tinkamam parengimui ir vėlesniam statybos vykdymui, pagal parengtą techninį darbo projektą bei atlieka projekto vykdymo priežiūrą. ● Projekto užbaigimu laikomas teigiamas Techninio darbo projekto ekspertizės aktas. Paslaugų apimtis: Visų privalomųjų tyrimų parengimas; Projektinių pasiūlymų parengimas, visuomenės informavimas (apmoka projektuotojas); Statybą leidžiančio dokumento gavimas; Techninio darbo ir Tvarkybos darbų projektų parengimas. Techninis darbo projektas: • Bendroji dalis; • Sklypo plano dalis; • Architektūrinė dalis; • Konstrukcijų dalis; • Elektrotechnikos apšvietimas dalis; • Elektrotechnikos dalis (ESO) (pagal poreikį); • Paveldosaugos dalis; • Apsauginės signalizacijos, stebėjimo kameros; • Pasirengimo statybai ir statybos darbų organizavimo dalis; • Statybos skaičiuojamosios kainos nustatymo dalis. • Kitos būtinos dalys, kurias, įvertinęs projektuojamų statinių specifiką, specialiuosius, reikalavimus ir prisijungimo sąlygas, Projektuotojas suderina su Statytoju (Užsakovu). title: Finland – Maintenance of information technology software – Rajatarkastussovelluksen (Ratas) ylläpidon hankinta
description: Rajavartiolaitos (myöhemmin myös Hankintayksikkö) kilpailuttaa Ratas-järjestelmän ylläpito- ja kehittämispalvelut. Ratas-järjestelmä on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 1 "ylläpidettävän kohteen kuvaus". Ratas on käytössä oleva tietojärjestelmäkokonaisuus, jonka toiminnan jatkuvuus, käytettävyys, tietoturvallisuus ja hallittu kehittäminen ovat keskeisiä hankintayksikön toiminnan kannalta. Järjestelmää on kehitetty vaiheittain nykyisen toimintamallin mukaisesti. Tulevan kilpailutuksen tavoitteena on muodostaa pitkäjänteinen palvelumalli, jolla varmistetaan järjestelmän laadukas ylläpito sekä mahdollistetaan tarpeelliset muutokset ja jatkokehitys hallitusti. Hankinnan ensisijaisena tavoitteena on varmistaa: • järjestelmän jatkuva käytettävyys ja toimintavarmuus • tehokas häiriönhallinta ja ongelmanratkaisu • järjestelmän teknisen ympäristön ylläpito • tietoturvallinen ja hallittu muutosten toteuttaminen • tarvittavan dokumentaation ja osaamisen säilyminen • tilaajan tukeminen järjestelmän elinkaaren hallinnassa. Palvelu sisältää alustavasti seuraavia kokonaisuuksia: Ylläpitopalvelut • järjestelmän jatkuva ylläpito • häiriöiden vastaanotto, analysointi ja ratkaisu • palvelupyyntöjen käsittely • ongelmanhallinta • versio- ja muutostenhallinta • käyttöympäristön tekninen ylläpito • yhteistyö infrastruktuuri- ja muiden toimittajien kanssa. Sovellustuki ja tekninen hallinta • sovelluksen teknisen toiminnan varmistaminen • sovelluskomponenttien hallinta • tekninen selvitys- ja asiantuntijatuki • suorituskyvyn ja kapasiteetin seuranta • tietoturvallisuuden ylläpito. Jatkokehitys ja muutokset • pienimuotoiset kehitystoimenpiteet • korjaavat ja ennakoivat muutokset • toiminnalliset kehitystarpeet • tekninen velanhallinta. Varsinainen kehitystyö ei ole hankinnan pääasiallinen tavoite, vaan sen tarkoituksena on tukea järjestelmän elinkaaren hallintaa ja ylläpitopalvelun onnistumista. Jatkokehityksen osuus palvelussa on ylläpitoa täydentävä osa-alue. Sen tavoitteena on mahdollistaa tarvittavat muutokset, korjaukset ja rajatut kehitystarpeet ilman erillisiä raskaita järjestelyjä. Ratas-järjestelmää on tarkoitus jatkokehittää tulevien vuosien aikana integraatiolla European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS) -järjestelmään ja uusimalla Ratas-järjestelmän käyttäjätunnistus nykyaikaisella ratkaisulla. Osallistumispyynnön tavoitteena on tunnistaa markkinoilta rajattu määrä ehdokkaita, joilla on riittävä osaaminen ja kapasiteetti vastata Ratas-järjestelmän ylläpito- ja kehittämispalvelusta. Ratas-järjestelmä tullaan korvaamaan nykyisen suunnitelman mukaan ensi vuosikymmenen puolella. Korvaavan järjestelmän hankinnan yksityiskohdat ovat vielä päättämättä.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Rosebud Lift Station Construction
description: The existing lift station has been in place since the early 1990s. Since its creation the hospital anticipates increased expansion in the emergency department, added on Tribal programs (dialysis, detox, Tribal Health Administration Building), added on 19 more quarters units, and is anticipating adding an additional 23 quarters units. The existing pumps are facing replacement every 1-2 years due to the unanticipated growth, but due to the growth we need to consider increasing the capacity of the wet well. In addition to switching from standard submersible pumps to chopper pumps to accommodate the random objects that get flushed into the system. In July both pumps ended up failing and they had to not only replace the pumps but pay for sewage disposal to circumvent overflow. A separate project is in the works to begin remediating/replacing damaged sewer mains due to inflow and infiltration. This construction solicitation will require the full removal and replacement of the lift station for the Rosebud complex. The existing lift station provides wastewater service to the hospital quarters units, and several tribal program buildings. Once installation is complete the new lift station will take the full sanitary load for the area currently being serviced by the existing lift station and be sized to handle expansion in the future. Then the existing lift station consisting of the wet well, dry well, pumps and piping will be demolished. The new lift station will consist of a wet well, a dry well, installation of chopper pumps, and force main connection. This project will also include a new control system to allow the facility to monitor flow into the lift station and the status of the equipment. Brand Names: Where brand names are referenced, they establish a standard of quality and performance. Offerors may propose equal products that meet or exceed the specified functional and performance requirements. The Government will evaluate equality based on technical compatibility, performance, and integration with the system.

title: $300M Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) Program at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM)
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Sources Sought Notice and Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). There are no bid packages, solicitations, specifications, or drawings available with this announcement. It does not constitute a procurement commitment by USACE, implied or otherwise. No contract will be awarded from this Sources Sought Notice. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. No reimbursement will be made for any cost associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow-up information requests. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way and will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal if a solicitation is issued in the future. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential contractors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to contractors regarding their submissions. Additional information may be requested after initial response, either from individual respondents or all respondents. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, on behalf of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), is conducting market research to support acquisition of an estimated $300M MATOC to support Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) construction efforts. This Market Research will help USACE determine the availability and capabilities of firms working within this NAICS code. The responses to this Notice will also be used to help determine whether a small business or socio-economic set-aside may be suitable to apply to this potential procurement. 3. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION The purpose of this MATOC will be to support primarily general construction activities at JBLM and its sub-installations (Lewis Main, McChord Field, and Yakima Training Center), including but not limited to renovation, repairs, minor building expansions and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), preventative maintenance, environmental abatement, erosion control and earthwork. The JBLM FSRM Program includes operational facilities, training sites, administrative spaces, barracks/troop housing, utility infrastructure systems (HVAC, electrical, fire protection), and site work for JBLM Garrison facilities. Projects will span multiple facility types across JBLM. Task Orders under this MATOC are primarily intended to provide a timely procurement response to general construction work such as remediation of facilities, e.g., maintenance, repair, asbestos and lead-based paint abatement, and minor construction situations relating to but not limited to: civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and anti-terrorism and force protection. Projects will be primarily general construction activities including but not limited to renovation, repairs, building expansions, and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), or repair by replacement. Scope may also include preventative maintenance, environmental abatement (e.g., asbestos and lead-based paint abatement), erosion control, and earthwork. Construction situations may include but are not limited to civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), fire protection systems, communications systems, and anti-terrorism and force protection. The MATOC may also be used for Task Orders expected to require some Incidental Design Work or extension of design effort by the Contractor, to include, but not be limited to fire alarm systems, fire sprinkler systems, HVAC system installation and balancing, communications systems, structural design of minor facilities or components and licensed professional engineer certification of site adaptation of pre-engineered structures. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The USACE Seattle District intends to award a MATOC to offerors determined to be qualified in accordance with the evaluation criteria. Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $300 Million ordering capacity, shared among all MATOC contractors. Structure: Qualified firms will be issued a MATOC contract, establishing a pool of multiple contractors available to support JBLM FSRM. Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with a single two (2) year option period. Exercise of options is at the Government's discretion. Project Size and Task Order Limits: The project size for Task Orders under this MATOC are anticipated to be between $250,000.00 and $25,000,000.00, and the average project duration is expected to be between six months to two years. Based on previous similar contracts, the occurrence of Task Orders may be frequent, especially in emergency situations, and during the 3rd and 4th quarters of the Government�s fiscal year. Project Delivery Methods: Projects will primarily be executed using Design-Bid-Build project delivery, with task orders representing the construction portion of project delivery. Task Order Selection: Competition for task orders will be held among all MATOC participants. Source selection methods will be determined for individual projects and may include various prices, performance, schedule or other trade-offs on the best-value spectrum. 5. ANTICIPATED INDUSTRY DAY USACE Seattle District anticipates hosting an Industry Day in the JBLM area on or about 15 October 2026. Exact date, time, location, registration instructions, and agenda will be published (SAM.gov and/or direct distribution to respondents to this RFI) later. Firms that respond to this RFI will be prioritized for Industry Day communications. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are requested to submit responses by completing the online questionnaire at: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/k6LtDRMKPP The questionnaire is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market research needed for determining the number and availability of contractors interested in this acquisition. Interested parties are also asked to submit a brief capabilities statement containing relevant information not otherwise addressed in the questionnaire. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 20 September 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. John McGuire, Contract Specialist Jeffrey Ross, Contracting Officer JBLM Special Projects Branch Contracting Division, Seattle District, Northwestern Division Email: john.e.mcguire@usace.army.mil Subject line: �Sources Sought Response � JBLM FSRM MATOC $300M � [Firm Name]� The Government welcomes candid industry feedback, recommendations, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this program. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

The MATOC may also be used for Task Orders expected to require some Incidental Design Work or extension of design effort by the Contractor, to include, but not be limited to fire alarm systems, fire sprinkler systems, HVAC system installation and balancing, communications systems, structural design of minor facilities or components and licensed professional engineer certification of site adaptation of pre-engineered structures. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The USACE Seattle District intends to award a MATOC to offerors determined to be qualified in accordance with the evaluation criteria. Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $300 Million ordering capacity, shared among all MATOC contractors. Structure: Qualified firms will be issued a MATOC contract, establishing a pool of multiple contractors available to support JBLM FSRM. Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with a single two (2) year option period. Exercise of options is at the Government's discretion. title: PACA Special Audits RFQ
description: The purpose of this Amendment 01 to Request for Quote (RFQ) F41999-27-Q-0007 for the AFSVC PACA Audit is to as follows: 1.PACA Audit RFQ F41999-27-Q-0007 - Questions & Answers are hereby added to the solicitation. 2.Offeror Letter - PACA Special Audits (13NOV26) is hereby replaced with Offeror Letter - PACA Special Audits (17NOV26). 3.ATCH 01 Instructions to Contractors (3NOV26) is hereby replaced with ATCH 01 Instructions to Contractors (17NOV26). 4.ATCH 14 is now the PACA Audit RFI Questions & Answers 5.ATCH 15 NAF Standard Clauses Incorporated By Reference Full Text 30 May 2025 is hereby added to the solicitation. 6.The solicitation closing date is hereby changed from Monday, 23 November 2026, 4:00 PM CT to now read: Tuesday, 1 December 2026, 4:00 PM CT. Please ensure you review all amended attachments and the Q&A responses carefully prior to submission. Please acknowledge receipt of this Amendment 01 below & return it in your File #1 Contract Documentation. General The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians, and families. Air Force Services Center supports bases, major commands (MAJCOMs), and the Air Staff by providing technical expertise, launching new initiatives, developing programs and operational procedures, and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures the successful operation of essential food services, fitness and sports centers, childcare and youth programs, lodging accommodations, and recreational opportunities for military members and their families worldwide. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field, and developing new programs supporting installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) centrally manages and administers the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program, which supports a worldwide mission providing independent oversight of internal controls, cash management, asset protection, and financial management across the enterprise. Background Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families, and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery, operational readiness, and the protection of government interests. Regular independent audits are required to evaluate the financial condition, control environments, and operational efficiencies of Nonappropriated Fund operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations Branch (AFSVC/VFSF) exercises central program oversight to ensure compliance with annual statutory audit requirements under Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 7600.06, Audit of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities and Related Activities, ensuring adequate audit coverage is provided across the enterprise for Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The term "Activities" refers to operational and revenue-generating entities within the Air Force structure. Audit engagements under this Special Audits contract specifically include financial statement audits and performance audits covering: � Accounting practices and transactional compliance; � Internal control environments and segregation of duties; � Cash management, vault operations, and electronic banking; � Fixed asset accountability, tracking, and depreciation; � Inventory valuation, spoilage controls, and physical counts; � Food and beverage operations and food service portfolios; � Centralized shared service center processing; � Venture gaming and electronic slot machine operations; � Supplemental mission dining operations; and � Agreed-upon procedures and special interest compliance reviews. Specific Focus Areas for the PACA Special Audits Program: � A. Shared Service Center (SSC): Conduct performance audits of the Shared Service Center (SSC) at the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) located in San Antonio, TX. The primary objective of the performance audit is to address economy, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The scope includes core accounting transaction workflows, inter-entity cost allocation methodologies, compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operational metrics, and the adequacy of financial management technology system controls. Further details will be outlined in specific delivery order project assignments. � B. Department of the Air Force (DAF) Venture Gaming Program: The DAF Venture Gaming Program operates electronic gaming and slot machine activities at authorized overseas military installations. The program serves as an important nonappropriated revenue generator utilized directly to support and enhance Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs across all Air Force installations. Authorized by DoDI 1015.10 and centrally managed by AFSVC in San Antonio, TX, slot machine operations present unique risks due to regulatory complexities, high cash volumes, and potential for manipulation. Scope includes electronic gaming data systems, meter reconciliations, cash drop and count controls, payout authorizations, jackpot disbursements, internal control safeguards against manipulation or theft, and compliance with federal tax reporting requirements (including IRS Form W-2G processing). � C. Air Force Cadet Dining Fund: The Cadet Dining Fund is a Supplemental Mission Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) operated by the 10th Force Support Squadron (10th FSS) located at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), Colorado. Supplemental Mission NAFIs receive nonappropriated funds generated from installation mission programs (training, food service, education, security). While congressionally appropriated funds (APF) cover civilian management, custodial services, and facility upkeep, nonappropriated funds are utilized strictly for food purchases and the operational maintenance of cadet meal operations. The fund provides daily dining support for over 4,400 cadets. The Contractor shall perform comprehensive financial statement and operational compliance audits examining food supply procurement, inventory receiving and storage controls, cost-per-meal accounting, meal card verifications, and financial statement accuracy in accordance with USAFAI 34-104 and applicable NAF regulations. � D. Commander�s Special Interest Audits: To address immediate, unplanned operational needs, the Government requires the capacity to execute ad hoc, targeted investigations known as Commander�s Special Interest Audits. These audits may be requested at any given time by Installation Commanders, the AFSVC Commander, or higher headquarters to address immediate operational concerns, suspected material control failures, or strategic risk areas. These ad hoc engagements may encompass any Air Force Installation, NAF Activity, or fund within the scope of this contract, and will be ordered and executed as individual, consolidated performance audit task orders in accordance with the established deliverables and pricing schedules. Scope Air Force Services Center requires the audit services of licensed Certified Public Accountants (CPAs) or CPA firms to perform financial statement audits of Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) financial statements and performance audits of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Services activities, with particular emphasis on high-risk areas identified through preliminary risk assessments and annual selection matrices.

title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) PEO-SDA
description: SAM.GOV Special Notice Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) H9241525X0001 US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) PEO SOF Digital Applications (SDA) SECTION 1 � INTRODUCTION 1.1 USSOCOM Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L) seeks to accelerate the application of commercially derived software innovation into deployable warfighting capabilities in support of Special Operations Forces (SOF). Early identification of warfighter needs and continuous engagement with users during software development and fielding will support increased lethality and efficiency. 1.2 In order to support rapid fielding of tailored software capabilities, SOF AT&L seeks to award FAR and non-FAR contracts and agreements to non-traditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects for Program Executive Office SOF Digital Applications (PEO SDA) that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of software intensive programs, platforms, components, algorithms, and processes. As such, under the authority of 10 USC � 3458 and DoD Class Deviation 2022-O0007, USSOCOM SOF AT&L releases this Commercial Solutions Opening. This CSO may result in an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) or a FAR-based contract. 1.3 This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will make awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2024 and 2025. Awards may include prototypes as well as concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile software development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. Interested vendors should note that all of PEO SDA�s Programs of Record are being managed in accordance with DoDI 5000.87, the software acquisition pathway, for the timely acquisition of custom software capabilities developed for the DoD. Programs will require government and contractor software teams to use modern iterative software development methodologies (e.g., agile or lean), modern tools and techniques (e.g., development, security, and operations (DevSecOps)), and human-centered design processes to iteratively deliver software to meet the users� priority needs. 1.3.1 Phase I: Solutions will be sought on a full-and-open basis under certain Technology Areas of Interest (AOI) relevant to SDA requirements. Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). SECTION 2 � GUIDELINES FOR SOLUTION BRIEFS, PITCHES, AND PROPOSALS 2.1 The purpose of the Solution Brief is to identify innovative solutions and preclude effort on the part of the Company whose proposed work may not be of interest to the Government. Companies are encouraged to follow the instructions detailed below. The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. The original of each submission received will be retained by USSOCOM and all other non-required copies destroyed. 2.3 Guidelines for Solution Brief Submissions: 2.3.1 It is generally desired that active Research and Development (R&D) and technology application is underway for potential solutions submitted under this CSO. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets] and each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: �

The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction, Subdivision 13 � Repair and Maintenance. title: Limited Source Delivery Order for Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Services under existing Basic Ordering Agreements � Order 5
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIRSYSCOM), acting under the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (PAE RAS) at Patuxent River, MD, intends to compete and award a limited source Firm Fixed Price (FFP) type Delivery Order. This order will be competed under one of four existing Basic Ordering Agreements (BOAs) to the below vendors for the procurement of Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Maritime Services: N0001925G1000: Insitu, Inc. (Insitu), East Columbia Way, Bingen, WA N0001926G1005: AeroVironment (AV), 900 Innovators Way, Simi Valley, CA N0001926G1006: Shield AI (Shield), 600 West Broadway, San Diego, CA N0001926G1007: Textron Systems (Textron), 124 Industry Lane, Hunt Valley, MD The delivery order will secure contractor-owned, contractor-operated UAS ISR services utilizing Maritime B-Kits #12 and #13 in support of multiple combatant commands. Contractors will be responsible for resources to produce sensor data, such as trained personnel, non-developmental UAS equipment, shipboard operations and logistics Conex containers, certifications, operation and maintenance, SpaceX Starshield SATCOM-capable hardware, spares, and product support. Contracted services would be in direct support of ISR missions requiring around-the-clock imagery and other sensor capability in support of those missions. It is anticipated that these services will support domestic and coalition military partners in combat and contingency operations based on Joint Urgent Operational Needs (JUONs), Fleet Top Level Requirements (TLR), and other operational requirements documents. The total period of performance includes a base period and four (4) option periods (to include environmental shock testing and training options) for up to 60 months of service. THIS NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. A determination by the Government to compete this procurement under the existing BOA, regardless of responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government will not pay for any responses received. There are no commitments by the Government to issue any solicitations, make an award or awards, or to be responsible for any monies expended by any interested parties before award of a contract for the efforts mentioned above. description: This project consists of roof and other maintenance work on the Mesa Falls Visitor�s Center on the Caribou-Targhee National Forest to provide deferred maintenance work. title: Research Triangle Park Forestry Sciences Laboratory HVAC Repair
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1240B27Q0025 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Research Triangle Park Forestry Sciences Laboratory HVAC Repair This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 238220 The small business size standard is $19 M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. The primary HVAC system (ACCU-1/VRV 2-7) for the Forest Science and Assessment Center (FSAC) is a Mitsubishi VRF system (BHM06227, Model PURY-P120TLMU-A, Serial 79W00897, 10 tons, R-410A) with 6 interior units. The system does not maintain condition set points and an initial evaluation during a preventative maintenance service call diagnosed with a potentially significant refrigerant leak. The Forestry Science Laboratory (FSL) building�s Fan Coil Units (FCUs) are redundant in the current HVAC system. The outside air vents are no longer needed and are introducing unconditioned air into the building. During cold weather, this can lead to the coils potentially freezing and have led to the freeze-stats tripping, resulting in nuisance shutdowns.

title: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar Creech AFB, Nevada Progressive Design-Build (PDB) with Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: DESCRIPTION The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Los Angeles District, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) / Market Intelligence Notice to obtain industry feedback regarding the anticipated design and construction of the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada, using Progressive Design-Build (PDB) under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, Other Transaction Authority for Construction. The purpose of this notice is to gather market intelligence regarding industry capabilities, experience, commercial practices, acquisition considerations, and potential challenges associated with the proposed project. Information obtained through this notice will assist the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, identifying potential industry participants, and refining project requirements prior to the release of the formal Program Solicitation. This notice is issued for informational and acquisition planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government to award an agreement. I. PURPOSE OF MARKET INTELLIGENCE USACE is conducting preliminary market intelligence to better understand industry capabilities and obtain feedback regarding the proposed use of Progressive Design-Build under an Other Transaction framework. The Government is particularly interested in receiving information regarding industry experience with progressive design-build delivery, design and construction of specialized military aviation facilities, anticipated project risks, acquisition considerations, and commercial practices that may improve project delivery. Participation in this market intelligence effort is voluntary. Responses will be used solely to support acquisition planning and development of the Government's proposed acquisition approach. II. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar Creech AFB, Nevada Project Location: Creech Air Force Base, Nevada Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Los Angeles District Program Amount (est.): $180M - $200M NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M Project Delivery Method: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) Acquisition Authority: 10 U.S.C. � 2808a � Other Transaction Authority for Construction III. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The proposed project consists of the design and construction of a Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Unit Operations and Hangar facility at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada. The project is anticipated to provide an approximately 84,931-square-foot facility consisting of a squadron command and operations center, aircraft maintenance unit, hangar bay, and associated aircraft parking apron to support CCA operations and aircraft maintenance activities. The project may include associated site improvements, utilities, infrastructure, and supporting facilities necessary to provide a complete and functional operational facility. The preliminary scope of work is subject to further development and refinement. Additional project requirements and technical information may be provided in future acquisition announcements. IV. ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION APPROACH The Government is considering the use of Progressive Design-Build (PDB) under the Other Transaction Authority for Construction pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Under the proposed approach, the Government anticipates utilizing a streamlined competitive selection process consisting of the following steps: Step 1 � White Papers / Statements of Qualifications Interested parties would submit qualification information demonstrating relevant experience, technical capabilities, management approach, and qualifications to perform the proposed project. Following evaluation of the submissions, the Government anticipates selecting a limited number of highly qualified firms to proceed to the next step. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations Selected firms would be invited to participate in pitch presentations to further demonstrate their qualifications, technical approach, and ability to successfully execute the proposed project. The Government anticipates selecting a preferred Progressive Design-Build Entity (PDBE) for negotiations regarding the initial agreement. Anticipated Post-Award Approach The proposed PDB approach would generally include two phases: Phase 1 � Design Development and Preconstruction Services: Collaborative development and refinement of the design, project requirements, construction approach, cost estimates, schedule, and associated preconstruction activities. Phase 2 � Final Design and Construction: Completion of the remaining design and construction activities, subject to successful negotiations, required approvals, and availability of funds. The final selection process, agreement structure, pricing methodology, and contractual arrangements will be established in the formal Program Solicitation and applicable agreement documents. V. MARKET INTELLIGENCE REQUESTED The Government is seeking input from interested industry participants regarding the proposed project and acquisition approach. Interested parties are encouraged to provide responses to the following questions: 1. Company Information and Capabilities Provide the company name, business address, primary point of contact, and a brief description of the firm's capabilities relevant to the proposed project. 2. Relevant Project Experience Describe your firm's experience with Progressive Design-Build or similar collaborative project delivery methods, particularly for military aviation facilities, hangars, or other complex construction projects. Also describe your firm�s (or proposed team�s) experience designing and constructing ICD 705-compliant spaces, including accreditation support. 3. Progressive Design-Build / OTA Experience Has your firm participated in projects utilizing Progressive Design-Build or Other Transaction agreements? If so, briefly describe your experience and identify any lessons learned. 4. Proposed Acquisition Strategy Does your firm have any recommendations or concerns regarding the proposed two-step selection process consisting of White Papers and Pitch Presentations? 5. Project Delivery and Risk Considerations What significant technical, design, construction, logistical, or scheduling challenges should the Government consider when developing the project requirements and acquisition strategy? Specifically address the following: Site-Specific Realities: Creech AFB is a remote desert location characterized by extreme temperatures, specialized airspace/base access constraints, and limited local labor and material resources. Key Drivers: Identify the primary cost and schedule drivers you foresee for this project. Mitigation Strategies: Describe your recommended risk mitigation and sourcing strategies to overcome these challenges. 6. Pricing and Commercial Practices What pricing approaches, cost development methods, and commercial practices would your firm recommend for a Progressive Design-Build agreement involving design development and subsequent construction? 7. Industry Participation Would your firm be interested in participating in the anticipated competition? If not, please identify any significant barriers to participation. 8. Additional Recommendations Provide any additional recommendations that may assist the Government in refining the project requirements, improving competition, managing risks, or developing the proposed PDB w/ OTA acquisition strategy. VI. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are encouraged to submit written responses addressing the market intelligence questions identified in Section V. Responses should be concise and limited to information relevant to the proposed project and acquisition approach. Respondents are requested to identify any proprietary or confidential business information included in their submissions. title: NOMEC and NOPP Partnership Forum
description: Request for Information (RFI) THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and market research planning purposes; it does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation. Furthermore, those who respond to this RFI should not anticipate feedback with regards to its submission; other than acknowledgment of receipt - ONLY IF a request for an acknowledgement is requested by the submitter. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is not seeking proposals at this time. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. All submissions become the property of the Federal Government, and will not be returned. Purpose of this RFI: The purpose of this RFI is to obtain detailed information from interested members of the public regarding opportunities to strengthen cross-sector partnerships in support of U.S. ocean mapping, exploration, and characterization priorities. Responses to this Request for Information (RFI) will inform development of the National Ocean Mapping, Exploration, and Characterization (NOMEC) and National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP) Partnership Forum on Building U.S. Ocean Technology and Data Partnerships to Advance Ocean Mapping, Exploration, and Characterization. In particular, the NOMEC Council and NOPP seek information regarding stakeholder priorities and capabilities; barriers to effective collaboration with the Federal Government; opportunities for enhanced cross-sector partnerships; and topics and activities that could support actionable outcomes from the Forum. NOAA is specifically looking for input as follows: Provide a high-level overview of your response to the attached document. This summary should articulate understanding of the RFI's primary objective and briefly outline the nature of the information, product, service, or capability being described. Describe the specialized technical teams, intellectual property (IP), or unique resources that would support the capabilities described in the attached document. Specified responses are requested in regards to Questions 1 through 9 of the attached document: Reference Question # - specific question or area of interest Respondent�s comprehensive response and detailed answer Please see the attached Attachment 1 Request for Information for specifics. Submission of Information: Interested parties are encouraged to submit a response which supports their claim that they have the qualifications and experience to provide services for one or more of the identified services. If there are areas of the requirement that your company and/or prospective team cannot meet, please identify those areas in your response along with amplifying information as to why your team cannot meet the government�s request. Specifically, any interested parties should provide the following information: Name of Company, address, and SAM.gov Unique Entity (UEID); Business type and designation (i.e., large business, small business, socioeconomic designation); Point of contact name, email, and phone number; Company website address; Any General Service Administration (GSA) schedule, Government Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC), or Multiple Award Contract numbers and information that may allow for streamlined procurement of services from your company; Do you currently have a contract(s) with any other Federal Agency for these types of services? Do you have a commercial catalog of products or systems similar to these services? RFI Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of submittals to this RFI, respondents are encouraged to prepare a response that closely adheres to the following format: The document format shall be either Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx), or Adobe Acrobat (.pdf) formats. Responses shall be prepared using 12 pt. font, 1-inch margins, and 8.5� by 11� paper and shall not exceed twenty (20) pages in length, including images, data displays, charts, graphs, and tables. It should be noted in the messaging of this RFI that participants should focus on their area of expertise to allow for diversity in responses. Respondents are encouraged to include any supporting material, such as data sheets or previous mission reports, as a separate attachment. Any such supporting material will be excluded from the page count. Response Deadline and Point of Contact Information: Responses to this notice should be documents attached to emails with the subject line �RFI Response - NOMEC and NOPP Partnership Forum� received no later than 3:00PM MT, Tuesday, December 1, 2026 to: Contract Specialist, Julia Hamilton at julia.l.hamilton@noaa.gov Contracting Officer, Angela Royster at angela.royster@noaa.gov The responses received will assist NOAA with identifying feasible technical solutions for this requirement. Each respondent, by submitting a response, agrees that any cost incurred by it in responding to this request, or in support of activities associated with this RFI, shall be the sole responsibility of the respondent. NOAA shall incur no obligations or liabilities whatsoever, to anyone, for any costs or expenses incurred by the respondent in responding to this RFI. Responses to this RFI will not be returned. Industry Discussions: Some respondents may be asked to provide additional information regarding the matters addressed in this RFI. Those respondents will be contacted directly if there is a need for further information. Questions: Respondents may submit questions regarding this RFI to the contact(s) listed above. Responses to questions may be posted on the Government Point of Entry. Please send any questions you may have to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer by no later than (NLT) 3:00PM MST, Friday, November 13, 2026. Each question shall provide the question number of the particular item being referred to in this RFI.

title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) PEO-SDA
description: SAM.GOV Special Notice Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) H9241525X0001 US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) PEO SOF Digital Applications (SDA) SECTION 1 � INTRODUCTION 1.1 USSOCOM Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L) seeks to accelerate the application of commercially derived software innovation into deployable warfighting capabilities in support of Special Operations Forces (SOF). Early identification of warfighter needs and continuous engagement with users during software development and fielding will support increased lethality and efficiency. 1.2 In order to support rapid fielding of tailored software capabilities, SOF AT&L seeks to award FAR and non-FAR contracts and agreements to non-traditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects for Program Executive Office SOF Digital Applications (PEO SDA) that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of software intensive programs, platforms, components, algorithms, and processes. As such, under the authority of 10 USC � 3458 and DoD Class Deviation 2022-O0007, USSOCOM SOF AT&L releases this Commercial Solutions Opening. This CSO may result in an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) or a FAR-based contract. 1.3 This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will make awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2024 and 2025. Awards may include prototypes as well as concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile software development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. Interested vendors should note that all of PEO SDA�s Programs of Record are being managed in accordance with DoDI 5000.87, the software acquisition pathway, for the timely acquisition of custom software capabilities developed for the DoD. Programs will require government and contractor software teams to use modern iterative software development methodologies (e.g., agile or lean), modern tools and techniques (e.g., development, security, and operations (DevSecOps)), and human-centered design processes to iteratively deliver software to meet the users� priority needs. 1.3.1 Phase I: Solutions will be sought on a full-and-open basis under certain Technology Areas of Interest (AOI) relevant to SDA requirements. Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). SECTION 2 � GUIDELINES FOR SOLUTION BRIEFS, PITCHES, AND PROPOSALS 2.1 The purpose of the Solution Brief is to identify innovative solutions and preclude effort on the part of the Company whose proposed work may not be of interest to the Government. Companies are encouraged to follow the instructions detailed below. The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. The original of each submission received will be retained by USSOCOM and all other non-required copies destroyed. 2.3 Guidelines for Solution Brief Submissions: 2.3.1 It is generally desired that active Research and Development (R&D) and technology application is underway for potential solutions submitted under this CSO. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets] and each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: �

title: Fort Eustis Dredge Material Management Area Construction in Newport News, Virginia
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Norfolk District, Corps of Engineers is contemplating a firm-fixed-price contract for the Design-Bid-Build construction of maintenance requirements at the Fort Eustis Dredge Material Management Area, located at JBLE � Eustis with provisions to include: Regrading/raising the disposal site berms to an elevation of 36 ft. The berms are currently at elevation 34 ft and have settled in a few places to below 34 ft. The work will also include the relocation of two existing spill boxes 50 � 60 feet into the disposal site. The existing access dirt and stone access ramp will need to be regraded, as well, to meet the new top-of-berm elevation. Offeror�s bonding capability (construction bonding level per contract and aggregate construction bonding level, both expressed in dollars). 4. Provide a narrative indicating the primary nature of your business. Narratives shall demonstrate experience in a similar type of work as described, at a similar contract value, and in a similar location. 5. If a specialty sub-contractor is used, the sub-contractor shall also provide work examples and experience. Based on definitions above, for each project submitted include: a.
